skill.name: deploying-postgres-k8s
skill.description: Deploy PostgreSQL on Kubernetes with CloudNativePG. Includes operator installation, HA cluster manifests, secrets, backups, monitoring, troubleshooting, and cleanup steps.
skill.summary: Guide CloudNativePG PostgreSQL deployments on Kubernetes.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby and shell backtick findings are false positives from Markdown fences, YAML examples, or inline formatting. Confirmed risks include hardcoded database URLs, commands that can reveal credentials, remote installation sources, and destructive cleanup commands.

remediation.suggestion: Replace inline DATABASE_URL and SQL password examples with Kubernetes Secret references or placeholder variables.
Avoid printing secret URI values in examples, or show redacted output and safer secret reference patterns.

remediation.issue: Remote manifest and Helm install sources
remediation.suggestion: Pin versions and ask users to review manifests or verify release artifacts before applying them.
Separate cleanup steps from normal operations and require explicit confirmation before deleting PVCs.

content.value_statement: Running PostgreSQL on Kubernetes requires operator setup, secrets, storage, backups, and troubleshooting. This skill provides CloudNativePG deployment steps for HA clusters, local development, and operations.
actual_capabilities: Shows direct manifest and Helm installation paths for the CloudNativePG operator.
Provides development and production cluster examples with storage, resources, and monitoring settings.
Explains CloudNativePG connection secrets and service endpoints for application deployments.
Covers psql access, database creation, migrations, and basic operational commands.
Includes S3 backup configuration and scheduled backup examples.
Lists monitoring, troubleshooting, and cleanup commands for common Kubernetes issues.
limitations: Does not provision a Kubernetes cluster, storage class, object bucket, or cloud credentials.
Does not replace managed PostgreSQL services such as RDS, Cloud SQL, Neon, or Supabase.
Includes example credentials that must be replaced with secure secrets before use.
Some commands require cluster administrator access and can change or delete resources.

use_cases.title: Create a local database lab
use_cases.description: Set up a single-instance PostgreSQL cluster for Kubernetes development and testing.

use_cases.title: Plan a production deployment
use_cases.description: Draft a CloudNativePG high-availability cluster with resource requests, storage, monitoring, and backups.

use_cases.title: Operate a running cluster
use_cases.description: Find commands for connection secrets, service endpoints, status checks, logs, backups, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Start a development cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the safest steps for deploying a single-instance CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster on my local Kubernetes cluster.

prompt_templates.title: Design an HA cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a three-instance CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster with storage, resource limits, anti-affinity, monitoring, and backup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Connect an application
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how my Kubernetes deployment should consume CloudNativePG connection secrets without hardcoding database credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and harden deployment steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security review before production use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my CloudNativePG deployment plan for secret handling, remote manifest risks, backup settings, and destructive cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: I need a PostgreSQL cluster for a staging Kubernetes namespace.
output: A staged plan that installs CloudNativePG, creates a small cluster, waits for readiness, and verifies service endpoints.
A note to replace all sample names, storage sizes, and credentials before applying the plan.

output_examples.input: How should my app connect to the database?
output: Guidance to use the CloudNativePG application secret and the read-write service for writes.
A warning to avoid copying plain database URLs into deployment manifests or shell history.

output_examples.input: My cluster is not becoming ready.
output: A troubleshooting checklist covering cluster status, pod placement, storage class availability, and controller logs.
Suggested next checks for PVC scheduling issues, service names, credentials, and replica lag.

best_practices: Review remote manifests and chart versions before applying them to a cluster.
Store database credentials in Kubernetes Secrets and avoid plain connection strings.
Test backup and restore procedures before relying on the cluster for production data.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder passwords into production manifests or migration commands.
Do not run cleanup commands against a production namespace without a verified backup.
Do not expose superuser connection strings to application deployments or shared logs.

faq.question: Does this skill install PostgreSQL automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples that a user or agent can follow with explicit permission.

faq.question: Which PostgreSQL operator does it use?
faq.answer: It uses CloudNativePG and references version 1.28 or newer in the source material.

faq.question: Can it be used with managed databases?
faq.answer: No. The skill is for PostgreSQL running inside Kubernetes, not hosted services such as RDS or Cloud SQL.

faq.question: Does it cover high availability?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a three-instance CloudNativePG cluster pattern with anti-affinity and monitoring options.

faq.question: Does it include backup guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows S3 object store backup settings, compression, retention, and scheduled backups.

faq.question: What should users review before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should review cluster context, namespace, storage class, remote manifest source, credentials, and cleanup risk.
